obligations.note: service.py is in scope. amend_memo still calls self._audit(actor, "amend_memo", "payment:{id}"), which records actor, action, target and time; the only change is a new log line before it.

The new call self._log.info("payment memo updated", payment_id=payment_id) matches the LOG-1 log-call pattern. By inspection it logs only the integer payment id, with no memo, payee or account data, so it adds no NPI to logs.
Ticket CHG-26236 is standard and was approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-15, before the change opened. Its components (payments.service) cover the only touched file, service.py.
Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver who is not the author (Linh Nguyen), gave a code_review approval.
The approval names head commit dc366e8f, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json claims ci-runner-02 ran on dc366e8f at 2026-10-17. The attached JUnit report says otherwise: it was produced on hostname dev-laptop-7.local, a developer workstation, and is timestamped 2026-10-23, after the 2026-10-19 review time. The report therefore cannot be the change's own CI run, and there is no valid evidence of the suite passing on the final commit.
The only touched component, payments.service, is not security_sensitive, so no security_review is required.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are changed, so no control_owner approval is required.
The change is not an emergency (ticket type standard, emergency=false), so no PIR is due.
The change relies on no exception. No product-obligation deviation was identified that would need one.
Ledger evidence covers payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, Approvals.java, Underwriting.java and Policy.java, none of which changed. No accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The code change is a single log line in LedgerService.amend_memo that logs only the payment id. It preserves the audit call and introduces no NPI logging, and ticket, independent approval and approval-on-head are all in order. However, the CI evidence is invalid. The JUnit report attached as the change's CI run comes from a developer Mac and is timestamped after the review time, contradicting run.json's claim of a ci-runner-02 run on the head commit. Without credible proof that the full suite and control tests pass on the final commit, CHG-4 fails, so the change is rejected. Separately, the description says unit tests were updated, but the diff touches no tests.
